pk.context: 10 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

clues.kinetics: Bioavailability is about 40%; a high-fat meal cuts Cmax by 29% and leaves AUC unchanged. Protein binding is 20%, and 28.5% of the dose is excreted unchanged by active renal secretion.
clues.substance: A white or almost white crystalline powder with a molecular weight of 285.69. It is stable at neutral and slightly basic pH.
clues.product: An NDA product supplied as 10 mg tablets, dispensed as one box for each treatment cycle.
clues.safety: Boxed warning for malignancy and teratogenicity. Contraindicated with current malignancy, in pregnant women and in HIV infection; upper respiratory tract infection and headache are the most common reactions.
clues.indication: Relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis in adults, including relapsing-remitting disease and active secondary progressive disease.
clues.mechanism: Its mechanism is not fully known, but it is thought to be cytotoxic to B and T lymphocytes by impairing DNA synthesis.

tell: A prodrug activated inside lymphocytes by phosphorylation, this purine antimetabolite carries a boxed malignancy warning.
